samples.summary: Find-bar replace mutates the CRDT through `editor.getDoc()` / `getStore()`, bypassing every read-only gate; the component is rendered in read-only mounts and receives no `readOnly` prop
samples.evidence: `editor.ts:4014` neutralizes the read-only write boundary by overwriting an allowlist of `MUTATING_METHODS` on the returned `api` (undo/redo/insertTable/insertLink/paste/…). `DocsFindBar` deliberately does not go through any of them: it constructs `new FindReplaceState(editor.getDoc(), () => editor.getStore().snapshot())` (docs-find-bar.tsx:54-57) and calls `state.replaceActive(replacement)` (line 125) / `state.replaceAll(replacement)` (line 134) straight against the live `Doc`. Neither call site checks `readOnly`, the component takes no `readOnly` prop, and `docs-view.tsx:599-606` renders it unconditionally for viewer mounts (`initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly)` at docs-view.tsx:327). The diff both adds code to these two functions and institutionalizes the bypass in prose ("bypassing the editor's own mutation entry points", docs-find-bar.tsx:118-120; docs-image-editing.md "run straight against the `Doc` the find bar holds"). Attacker path: a viewer on an anonymous share link who reaches the replace row writes to the shared Yorkie tree; per `docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:292` and `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:87`, the server-side auth webhook defaults to shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset ⇒ allow), so the client flag is the effective write boundary. I could not complete the chain to a supported UI entry point: `showReplace` is only set by `onFindReplaceRequest`, whose only trigger is Cmd/Ctrl+H at `text-editor.ts:1072-1076`, which the `readOnly` early-return at `text-editor.ts:894-912` blocks — hence medium confidence. The gate is nonetheless absent at the mutation itself, so any future entry point (menu item, toolbar, deep link, or a state change that sets `findBarShowReplace`) is an unguarded write.

samples.summary: The read-only `MUTATING_METHODS` allowlist is bypassable by design because `EditorAPI.getDoc()` / `getStore()` are exposed on read-only mounts too
samples.evidence: `editor.ts:4014-4032` enumerates mutating API methods and replaces them with no-ops when `readOnly`, with the comment "the programmatic EditorAPI … is reachable by any holder of `api`, so gate it here too". The same `api` object hands out `getDoc()` and `getStore()` ungated, which give unrestricted write access to the document and the undo store — exactly the seam `DocsFindBar` uses (docs-find-bar.tsx:54-57, 125, 134). An allowlist that can be side-stepped by two unlisted accessors reads as covered while offering no enforcement; anyone adding a mutating helper outside `editor.ts` inherits no gate. Hardening: gate the write surface at `Doc`/store level for read-only mounts, or return a read-only façade from `getDoc()`/`getStore()`.

samples.summary: Removing the `readOnly` early return from `handleImageMouseDown` lets a viewer focus the hidden textarea, widening the read-only attack surface onto guards that were previously unreachable
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` no longer returns on `readOnly` (the diff deletes `if (readOnly) return;`), and the image-body branch now calls `selectImageInline` (editor.ts:1255-1259) which calls `textEditorRef?.focus()`. Before this change a read-only mount deliberately never focused the hidden textarea (`if (!readOnly) textEditor.focus()`, editor.ts:2919), so its keyboard/IME/clipboard handlers were effectively unreachable for a viewer. They now are. I traced each and found them guarded — `handleInput` (text-editor.ts:768), `handleCompositionStart` (692), `handlePaste` (1473), `handleCut` (1237), `handleKeyDown` (894), `insertText` (639), and the image paths `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2311), `handleImageResizeMouseMove` (2496), `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (2534) — so I have no working bypass. Reported because the change makes that whole guard set load-bearing where it previously was not, and because `readOnly` is the effective write boundary while the Yorkie auth webhook defaults to shadow mode (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:87). Any future handler added to the textarea without a `readOnly` check is now a viewer-reachable write.

samples.summary: None of the three new/relied-on `readOnly` gates on the image-resize path is pinned by a test, so an authorization regression there would stay green
samples.evidence: The change makes read-only image selection reachable and then relies on three separate `readOnly` gates to stop a viewer's CRDT write: the handle branch (`editor.ts:2626`), `handleImageResizeMouseMove` (2496) and `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (2534). `packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts` drives read-only selection only through the `selectImageAt` API and a miss-everything mousedown; no test performs a handle drag, so deleting any one of the three gates turns no test red. The branch's own task note concedes this ("Known coverage gap", 20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md). Because the client `readOnly` flag is the effective write boundary under the default shadow-mode auth webhook, an untested auth gate is a silent-regression risk rather than a style issue.
searchedFor: grep for handleImageResizeMouseMove / mousemove / mouseup drags in packages/docs/test
read of the read-only sections of the new test file in the diff

verdict.reason: The mutation site is real (docs-find-bar.tsx:54-57, 121-137 mutate the Doc via getDoc/getStore, which are not in the editor.ts:4015-4025 MUTATING_METHODS allowlist, and the component gets no readOnly prop at docs-view.tsx:599-606). But the replace controls are unreachable in read-only mounts: the replace row renders only under `showReplace` (docs-find-bar.tsx:277); `findBarShowReplace` is set true at exactly one place, docs-view.tsx:431-432 inside `onFindReplaceRequest`; that callback has exactly one invocation repo-wide, text-editor.ts:1072-1076 (`Mod+H`); and the read-only early return at text-editor.ts:894-912 discards every non-navigation key except Mod+A and Mod+F, so Mod+H hits `return` at line 909 and never fires. No synthetic keydown dispatch or alternate producer exists (grep for setFindBarShowReplace, onFindReplaceRequest, replaceActive/replaceAll shows single call sites). The only read-only DocsView mount is shared-document.tsx:306-311 with `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (line 278) constant for the mount, so no false→true flip can leave a live replace row; docs-detail.tsx:216 passes no readOnly at all. Server-side enforcement also exists and denies `rw` for viewer share links (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:196-200); the shadow-mode default (lines 86-87, 97-105) is a separate documented rollout posture. What remains is defense-in-depth hardening at an unreachable site, not an exploitable authorization bypass.

finding.summary: Server-side write authorization for viewer share links is shadow-mode by default, so the client `readOnly` flag this change widens is the only effective write boundary
finding.evidence: `YorkieAuthController` computes the per-document read/write decision but returns ALLOW whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (constructor at :86-88, shadow branch at :97-105); packages/backend/README.md:111 documents `false` as the default. `readOnly` in the frontend is derived purely client-side (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152`, `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`) and passed into `initialize()`. In a default deployment, therefore, any client-side read-only gap in the docs editor is a real write for an anonymous viewer, not a UX inconsistency. This is pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the assumption the change under review leans on: the diff deliberately opens `handleImageMouseDown`, the textarea focus and the key/clipboard handlers to viewers and compensates entirely with client-side `readOnly` checks (the design doc it adds says so explicitly at docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:292). Reported so the widened surface is weighed against the enforcement posture rather than assumed to be backstopped by the server.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the repository. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88 gates enforcement on YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true', and :97-105 discards any deny decision in shadow mode, returning HTTP 200 with allowed:true. The only viewer/editor role distinction (hasAccess :200, `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) is therefore computed and thrown away. Shadow is the documented default (packages/backend/README.md:111-114, :186-188), and a grep of the entire non-docs tree found no deployment/env file setting the flag to 'true', so a stock deployment is unenforced; docs/tasks/archive/2026/08/20260810-notifications-lessons.md:20-22 independently records that untrusted clients can attach to arbitrary doc keys while enforcement is off. Meanwhile readOnly is derived purely client-side (shared-document.tsx:278) and forwarded into packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:919, where every write gate is a local boolean branch (2311, 2496, 2534, 2626, 2715, 2723, 4014) that an attacker driving the Yorkie SDK directly never executes. Net effect: an anonymous viewer-role share-link holder can obtain a Yorkie token and perform rw writes, a viewer-to-editor privilege escalation. This is a weakened permission gate moved out of the enforced path — in-lane for the security rubric. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no alternative server-side role check guards Yorkie writes, and pre-existing/out-of-diff status does not exempt a real access-control defect.
